the flows named (project creation, workbench, model serving, pipelines) align with its documented role. | ", "artifacts/epic-tasks/RHAISTRAT-9017-E001.md": "--- epic_id: RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 title: Keyboard accessibility remediation for the four audited Dashboard flows parent_strat: RHAISTRAT-9017 component: Dashboard team: RHOAI Dashboard type: Implementation priority: P1 dependencies: [] ai_signals: change_specificity: 1 pattern_precedent: 1 adapter_pattern: 0 existing_foundation: 1 open_questions: 1 external_dependency: 1 human_process_gates: 0 repo_access: 1 architecture_claims: 1 implementation_type: null investigation_signals: null ai_implementability: High ai_implementability_score: 7 jira_key: «redacted» null gated_by: null gate_failure_impact: null --- # Keyboard accessibility remediation for the four audited Dashboard flows ## Description This epic makes the four audited core Dashboard flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission) fully operable by keyboard alone and gives them consistent, visible focus indicators. The accessibility audit enumerated the exact defects per flow — focus lost in modals, unreachable controls, and inconsistent focus indicators — and this epic remediates those defects in the Dashboard. ## Scope - Fix keyboard operability defects in the four audited flows so every control is reachable and operable by keyboard, with no focus traps: - Project creation flow - Workbench spawn flow - Model deployment flow - Pipeline run submission flow - Restore and maintain logical focus in modals and dialogs used by these flows (focus moves into the modal on open, stays trapped while open as appropriate, and returns to the triggering control on close). - Apply consistent visible focus indicators across all controls in the audited flows, matching the established pattern used elsewhere in the Dashboard. - Verify each flow end-to-end using keyboard-only navigation. Out of scope: screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require, and flows outside the four audited ones. ## Acceptance Criteria - Each of the four audited flows can be completed start-to-end using only the keyboard, per the audit report's enumerated defects: every defect listed for that flow is fixed or explicitly dispositioned. - No focus traps or keyboard-unreachable controls remain in the four audited flows, verified by a keyboard-only walkthrough of each flow. - Focus indicators are visible and consistent across all interactive controls in the audited flows. - Focus behavior in modals is correct: focus enters the modal on open, remains within it while open, and returns to the invoking control on dismiss. - Existing functional behavior of the four flows is unchanged (remediation only; no feature changes). ## HLR Traceability - **HLR-1** (P1): The four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard, with no focus traps or unreachable controls. - **HLR-2** (P1): Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited flows. Two public-sector customers require an updated, published conformance statement before renewal, so the published documentation is a first-class deliverable of this strategy, not an incidental touch-up. ## Scope - Revise the VPAT entries for the four remediated core flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission) to reflect the keyboard operability and focus-indicator fixes, marking the supported criteria accurately. - Update the product documentation accessibility statement to describe the current conformance state of the audited flows. - Republish the updated VPAT and accessibility statement through the normal documentation release process. Content outline (inside Scope, per artifact contract): 1. VPAT revision per audited flow: keyboard operability and focus-visible support status, with notes on any remaining known limitations. 2. Accessibility statement refresh: current conformance summary, scope of the audit remediation, and contact/reporting path for accessibility issues. 3. Republication of both artifacts. ## Acceptance Criteria - The VPAT accurately reflects the remediated state of the four audited flows: each claim in it is consistent with the implemented keyboard behavior and focus indicators. - The accessibility statement in the product documentation is updated to describe the fixed state. - Both documents are technically reviewed against the implemented behavior by the engineering owners of the Dashboard fixes (per HLR-3's technical-review requirement), with review sign-off recorded. - The updated VPAT and accessibility statement are republished and publicly available. - No conformance claim in either document overstates the implemented state. ## HLR Traceability - **HLR-3** (P2): The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect the fixed state, with technical review. The docs-authoring epic required by the documentation deliverable is present. No conditional branches are needed (no bounded uncertainties).
